You are a coding agent. Today's date is 2026-10-12.
Write a complete program that works with the latest released version of every library it uses, as installed today.
Do not use deprecated or removed APIs. If tools are available to you, first use them to look up the current version of each library and its changelog or migration guide, then write the code.
The program must run offline, finish on its own, and print its results.
End your reply with exactly one fenced code block that holds the whole program.

Using Pillow, create an 800x600 RGB image in memory, draw the text 'Hello' on it with the default font, measure the pixel width and height of that text, then resize the image to 200x150 with high-quality (Lanczos-style) downsampling. Print the text size and the final image size.

Target: Python 3.11, run as `python main.py`.

To accomplish this task, we use the `PIL.Image` and `PIL.ImageDraw` modules from the `Pillow` library. As of October 2026, the current version of Pillow is 11.x. The `Image.Resampling.LANCZOS` constant is the modern, non-deprecated way to perform high-quality downsampling (replacing the older `Image.ANTIALIAS` which was removed in Pillow 10.0.0).

The following program creates the image, calculates the text bounding box using `textbbox`, performs the resize, and outputs the requested dimensions.

```python
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

def main():
    # 1. Create an 800x600 RGB image in memory
    width, height = 800, 600
    image = Image.new("RGB", (width, height), color="white")
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)

    # 2. Draw the text 'Hello'
    # Using default font (load_default() is the standard way to get a basic font)
    font = ImageFont.load_default()
    text = "Hello"
    
    # Position the text at (10, 10)
    text_position = (10, 10)
    draw.text(text_position, text, fill="black", font=font)

    # 3. Measure the pixel width and height of the text
    # textbbox returns (left, top, right, bottom)
    bbox = draw.textbbox(text_position, text, font=font)
    text_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    text_h = bbox[3] - bbox[1]

    # 4. Resize the image to 200x150 with high-quality (Lanczos) downsampling
    # Image.Resampling.LANCZOS is the current standard for high-quality resizing
    resized_image = image.resize((200, 150), resample=Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)

    # 5. Print the results
    print(f"Text size: {text_w}x{text_h} pixels")
    print(f"Final image size: {resized_image.size[0]}x{resized_image.size[1]} pixels")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
